@graph.articleBody: Location targeting tells Google Ads where your ads can show. Choose the shape of your area (a radius of at least 1 km or named areas), check the broad Presence or Interest setting on purpose, and use Keyword Planner estimates before widening. Estimates are not guarantees.

mainEntity.name: What is the smallest radius I can use in Google Ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google states that radius targeting requires a radius of at least 1 km around any given location, which is a little over half a mile. If your real territory is smaller than that, consider named areas instead of a radius.

mainEntity.name: What does "Presence or Interest" mean in Google Ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the name Google gives its broad geo targeting. Google's page says it can help you reach people who not only exist in your targeted locations. Check which setting your campaign uses so you know who your area includes, and compare your leads against what you expected.

mainEntity.name: Should I target a radius or a city?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how your territory works. Use a radius when your limit is distance from your shop, and named areas when your limit follows borders such as city lines. Many businesses with one core area and a few extra towns mix the two.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if I am reaching the wrong people?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look at where your calls and form leads come from and compare that to the places you serve. If many come from outside your area, revisit the shape of your area and the targeting choice, and cut irrelevant searches with negative keywords.
